lessons.title: The Architecture of Mongolian Sentences: Head-Final SOV Word Order
lessons.cyrillicTitle: Recognize that modifiers precede heads and the finite predicate anchors the absolute end of the clause.
lessons.primaryPurpose: Introduce the canonical Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) sentence topology of Modern Mongolian.
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Recognize that modifiers precede heads and the finite predicate anchors the absolute end of the clause.
lessons.audioPurpose: Clear terminal falling intonation contours marking the end of SOV clauses.

grammarOverview.summary: Introduce the canonical Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) sentence topology of Modern Mongolian.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the scrambled word tokens into a grammatically correct Mongolian declarative sentence: 'I will read a book'.
exercises.hint: In Mongolian, the subject comes first, the direct object comes second, and the verb always stands at the end.
exercises.explanation: Mongolian is strictly head-final with canonical Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order. 'Би' (Subject) precedes 'ном' (Object), and 'уншина' (Verb) must terminate the clause.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! You placed the verb at the clause-final anchor.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Modern Mongolian strictly prohibits English-style SVO ordering (*Би уншина ном). The finite predicate holds the absolute right edge of the sentence.

exercises.prompt: In the sentence 'Багш маргааш сургууль дээр ирнэ' (The teacher will come to school tomorrow), which word occupies the finite predicate slot?
exercises.hint: Look at the final word of the sentence that conveys the action/tense.

options.explanation: Correct! 'Ирнэ' is the finite verb in clause-final position.
Incorrect. 'Багш' is the subject in initial position.
Incorrect. 'Маргааш' is a temporal modifier.
Incorrect. This is a postpositional locative phrase.

exercises.explanation: The finite verb 'ирнэ' (comes/will come) concludes the clause, serving as the syntactic head to which all preceding arguments link.

learnerFeedback.onFailure: The predicate in Mongolian is the verb at the very end: 'ирнэ'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Because Mongolian is head-final, modifiers (temporal, locative, direct objects) always precede the verb head, and attributive adjectives precede the noun head.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase correctly demonstrates the rule that demonstratives and descriptive adjectives must precede the head noun?

options.explanation: Correct! Demonstrative 'Энэ' + Adjective 'том' + Head noun 'гэр'.
Incorrect. Placing the noun before its modifiers violates head-final structure.
Incorrect. The demonstrative 'энэ' must precede the adjective.
Incorrect. Unnatural word order.

exercises.explanation: In Mongolian noun phrases, the hierarchy is strictly Demonstrative -> Adjective -> Head Noun ('Энэ том гэр').

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Сайн байна! Modifiers always precede the noun in Mongolian.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Remember: Demonstrative first, adjective second, noun last (Энэ том гэр).

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Unlike Romance languages where adjectives often follow the noun, Mongolic syntax requires all attributes to branch to the left of their head noun.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Assembling Complex Clause with Temporal & Locative Arguments
exercises.prompt: Reconstruct the scrambled words into a standard sentence: 'Dorj will arrive in the city today'.
exercises.explanation: Standard neutral Mongolian order is Subject + Temporal Adverbial + Locative Adverbial + Verb: 'Дорж өнөөдөр хотод ирнэ'.

learnerFeedback.onFailure: Follow the sequence: Дорж -> өнөөдөр -> хотод -> ирнэ.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Time expressions may optionally topicalize to the very front ('Өнөөдөр Дорж хотод ирнэ'), but the verb 'ирнэ' must unconditionally remain at the end.

exercises.exerciseTitle: Syntax Error Spotting: SVO Transfer Interference
exercises.prompt: A foreign learner wrote: '*Би ууна цай' (attempting to say 'I drink tea'). What is the error and how should it be corrected?
exercises.hint: The direct object 'цай' must come before the verb 'ууна'.

options.text: The verb 'ууна' was placed before the object; it should be 'Би цай ууна'.
options.explanation: Correct! English SVO was incorrectly transferred. Mongolian requires SOV: Би цай ууна.

options.text: The pronoun 'Би' is missing an accusative suffix.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Би' is the subject, correctly in the nominative.

options.text: 'Цай' is a loanword and cannot take an object position.
options.explanation: Incorrect. 'Цай' is perfectly normal native vocabulary.

exercises.correctAnswer: The verb 'ууна' was placed before the object; it should be 'Би цай ууна'.
acceptableAlternatives: The verb 'ууна' was placed before the object
exercises.explanation: In English, verbs precede their objects (I drink tea), but in Mongolian, the object must precede the verb: 'Би цай ууна'.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! SVO must be converted to SOV: 'Би цай ууна'.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Mongolian always puts the object before the verb: Би цай ууна.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: SVO transfer error is the single most common grammatical slip for beginning Mongolian learners from Indo-European language backgrounds.

lessons.audioPurpose: Professional radio announcer voice greetings recorded at natural tempo.

grammarOverview.summary: Expand time greetings into full formal performative sentences using 'хүргэе' (I convey).

exercises.exerciseTitle: Diurnal Greeting Matching: Time of Day to Salutation
exercises.prompt: It is 09:00 AM and you arrive at a Mongolian corporate office. What is the appropriate formal greeting?

options.explanation: Correct! 'Өглөөний мэнд' is the polite greeting for the morning hours.
Incorrect. 'Өдрийн мэнд' is used around midday and afternoon (12:00-17:00).
Incorrect. 'Оройн мэнд' is used in the evening (after 18:00).

options.text: Сайхан амраарай! (Have a good rest / Good night!)
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is a parting wish before sleeping.

exercises.explanation: 'Өглөөний мэнд хүргэе' (literally: 'I deliver the peace/wellbeing of the morning') is the standard formal greeting before noon.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! 'Өглөөний мэнд хүргэе' is used in the morning.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The greeting uses the genitive form of the time noun (өглөө -> өглөөний, өдөр -> өдрийн, орой -> оройн) modifying 'мэнд' (wellbeing), followed optionally by the performative verb 'хүргэе' (let me convey).

exercises.prompt: A senior colleague greets you at 14:00 with: 'Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе!'. How should you respectfully reply?
exercises.hint: Echo the diurnal greeting and add a respectful inquiry about their wellbeing using 'Та'.

options.text: Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе, та сайн байна уу? (Good afternoon, are you well?)
options.cyrillic: Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе, та сайн байна уу?
options.explanation: Correct! Echoing the time-specific greeting with the formal honorific inquiry 'та сайн байна уу?' is the polite gold standard.
Incorrect. 'Юу байна' is informal slang inappropriate with senior colleagues.

options.text: Баяртай, маргааш уулзъя. (Goodbye, see you tomorrow.)
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is a departure farewell, not an arrival greeting.

exercises.correctAnswer: Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе, та сайн байна уу? (Good afternoon, are you well?)
acceptableAlternatives: Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе, та сайн байна уу?
Өдрийн мэнд, та сайн байна уу?
exercises.explanation: Mongolian communicative etiquette requires matching or elevating the politeness register of a diurnal greeting with 'Та сайн байна уу?'.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Төгс! Respectful and culturally authentic response.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Reply politely with: 'Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе, та сайн байна уу?'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Addressing an equal or senior requires the polite 2nd-person pronoun 'Та' (never informal 'чи') in business and administrative settings.

audio.speechSynthesisText: Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе, та сайн байна уу?
audio.slowSpeechSynthesisText: Өдрийн мэнд хүргэе, та сайн байна уу?
audio.ipaTranscription: /ɵtʰriːn mentʰ xʊrɡiː, tʰa sæːŋ pæːn ʊː/

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct genitive time word to complete the 19:00 PM greeting: '______ мэнд хүргэе!'.
exercises.hint: Recall how time-of-day nouns take the genitive attribute ending -н to modify 'мэнд' (wellbeing) for dusk hours.
exercises.explanation: 'Оройн мэнд хүргэе!' means 'Good evening!'. The noun 'орой' adds -н to form the genitive attribute 'оройн'.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! 'Оройн мэнд хүргэе!' is complete.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Use the genitive form of 'орой' (evening) ending in -н: 'Оройн'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Nouns ending in short diphthongs or vowels like 'орой' add '-н' to form the unstable genitive attribute ('оройн мэнд').

exercises.exerciseTitle: Acoustic Salutation Decoding in Public Broadcast
exercises.prompt: Listen to the television news anchor opening the broadcast. At what time of day is this news program airing?
exercises.stimulusTextCyrillic: Эрхэм хүндэт үзэгчид ээ, энэ өдрийн амар амгаланг айлтган мэндчилье.
exercises.hint: Listen for 'энэ өдрийн' (of this day / afternoon).

options.explanation: Correct! The anchor said 'энэ өдрийн амар амгалан' (peace of this day/afternoon).
Incorrect. The anchor did not say өглөөний.
Incorrect. This is daytime broadcast greeting.

exercises.explanation: Anchors frequently use high-register ceremonial phrases like 'энэ өдрийн амар амгаланг айлтгая' for midday/afternoon transmissions.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Сайн байна! You caught 'энэ өдрийн' in formal broadcast speech.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: The anchor said 'энэ өдрийн' which refers to the day/afternoon.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: 'Амар амгаланг айлтгая' is a classical ceremonial formula deriving from traditional epistolary conventions.

audio.speechSynthesisText: Эрхэм хүндэт үзэгчид ээ, энэ өдрийн амар амгаланг айлтган мэндчилье.
audio.slowSpeechSynthesisText: Эрхэм хүндэт үзэгчид ээ, энэ өдрийн амар амгаланг айлтган мэндчилье.
audio.ipaTranscription: /erxəm xʊntət utsəktsʰət eː, en ɵtriːn amər amɢaɮəŋ aæɮtʰɢən mentʰtʃiɮjiː/

exercises.exerciseTitle: Register Appropriateness: Casual vs Formal Greetings
exercises.prompt: You meet your company CEO in the elevator. Which greeting demonstrates proper professional respect?
exercises.hint: Avoid one-word peer greetings like 'Сайн уу'. Use full polite time-of-day phrases.

options.text: Өглөөний мэнд хүргэе, захирал аа. (Good morning, Director.)
options.explanation: Correct! Formal diurnal greeting paired with respectful professional title + vocative particle.
Incorrect. This is overly familiar peer slang inappropriate for executive staff.
Incorrect. Highly colloquial phrasing.

exercises.correctAnswer: Өглөөний мэнд хүргэе, захирал аа. (Good morning, Director.)
exercises.explanation: Addressing company leadership requires formal time salutations ('Өглөөний мэнд хүргэе') and title honorifics ('захирал аа').

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! Dignified and respectful executive communication.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Use 'Өглөөний мэнд хүргэе, захирал аа.' for formal leadership.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The vocative enclitic 'аа/ээ/оо/өө' attached to titles ('захирал аа', 'багш аа') signals respectful direct address in administrative communication.

lessons.primaryPurpose: Simulate arriving at a business office or academic department and executing appropriate greeting rituals.
lessons.communicativeOutcome: Approach a reception desk, deliver time-appropriate formal salutations, and acknowledge the receptionist's reply.
lessons.audioPurpose: Authentic multi-speaker reception desk dialogue.

grammarOverview.summary: Simulate arriving at a business office or academic department and executing appropriate greeting rituals.

exercises.prompt: You step up to the reception desk. The receptionist smiles and says: 'Сайн байна уу? Танд юугаар туслах вэ?'. What should you say if you have an appointment with Mr. Bold?
exercises.stimulusTextCyrillic: Хүлээн авагч: Сайн байна уу? Танд юугаар туслах вэ?
exercises.hint: Use the comitative case '-тай' (with) when expressing meeting someone: Болдтой уулзах.

options.text: Сайн байна уу. Би Болд захиралтай уулзахаар ирсэн юм. (Hello. I have come to meet Director Bold.)
options.cyrillic: Сайн байна уу. Би Болд захиралтай уулзахаар ирсэн юм.
options.explanation: Correct! Natural and polite phrasing using intentional supine -хаар/хээр with comitative -тай.

options.text: Болд хаана байна? Би шууд орлоо. (Where is Bold? I'm going in directly.)
options.cyrillic: Болд хаана байна? Би шууд орлоо.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Impolite and violates visitor protocol.

options.text: Би захирал биш. (I am not a director.)
options.explanation: Incorrect. Irrelevant response.

exercises.correctAnswer: Сайн байна уу. Би Болд захиралтай уулзахаар ирсэн юм. (Hello. I have come to meet Director Bold.)
acceptableAlternatives: Сайн байна уу. Би Болд захиралтай уулзахаар ирсэн юм.
exercises.explanation: '[Name]-тай уулзахаар ирсэн' (I have come in order to meet [Name]) is the standard polite formula at Mongolian office receptions.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! Polite and accurate visitor phrasing.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Say: 'Сайн байна уу. Би Болд захиралтай уулзахаар ирсэн юм.'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The supine verbal noun in -хаар⁴ ('уулзахаар') denotes the deliberate purpose of arriving ('ирсэн').

audio.speechSynthesisText: Сайн байна уу. Би Болд захиралтай уулзахаар ирсэн юм.
audio.slowSpeechSynthesisText: Сайн байна уу. Би Болд захиралтай уулзахаар ирсэн юм.
audio.ipaTranscription: /sæːŋ pæːn ʊː. pʰi pɔɮtʰ tsaxʲirəɮtʰæː ʊːɮtsəxaːr irsəŋ jʊm/

exercises.prompt: The receptionist checks the register and says: 'За, та энд түр хүлээнэ үү. Би одоо мэдэгдье.' What did the receptionist ask you to do?
exercises.stimulusTextCyrillic: Хүлээн авагч: За, та энд түр хүлээнэ үү. Би одоо мэдэгдье.
exercises.hint: 'Түр' means 'temporarily/for a moment', and 'хүлээнэ үү' means 'please wait'.

options.text: Please wait here a moment while she notifies him.
options.explanation: Correct! 'Түр хүлээнэ үү' means 'please wait a moment'.

options.text: Please leave and come back next week.
options.explanation: Incorrect. She asked you to wait briefly.

options.text: Please call Director Bold on your phone right now.
options.explanation: Incorrect. She is notifying him herself.

exercises.correctAnswer: Please wait here a moment while she notifies him.
exercises.explanation: 'Түр хүлээнэ үү' is a polite request utilizing the volitional directive ending -нэ үү/нө үү ('will you please wait a moment').

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Зөв! The receptionist asked you to wait briefly.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: 'Түр хүлээнэ үү' = Please wait a moment.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The polite request marker '-нэ үү/-нэ үү' attaches to verb stems to form soft directives appropriate in service interactions.

audio.speechSynthesisText: За, та энд түр хүлээнэ үү. Би одоо мэдэгдье.
audio.slowSpeechSynthesisText: За, та энд түр хүлээнэ үү. Би одоо мэдэгдье.
audio.ipaTranscription: /tsa, tʰa entʰ tʰur xʊɮiːnə ʊː. pʰi ɔtɔː metəkjiː/

exercises.prompt: When the receptionist asks 'Та нэр, байгууллагаа хэлнэ үү?' (Could you please state your name and organization?), assemble your reply: 'I am a representative from ABC company'.
exercises.hint: Subject (Би) + Genitive company (ABC компанийн) + Predicate noun (төлөөлөгч).
exercises.explanation: Genitive modifiers precede the noun head: 'ABC компанийн төлөөлөгч' (ABC company's representative).

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Маш сайн! Accurate company affiliation phrasing.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Foreign corporate acronyms appear before the generic word 'компани', which carries the case suffix ('компанийн').

exercises.exerciseTitle: Acoustic Dialogue Extraction: Visitor Log Data
exercises.prompt: Listen to the receptionist give directions to the visitor: 'Болд захирлын өрөө 3-р давхарт, 305 тоот.' On which floor and in which room number is the meeting?

options.explanation: Correct! '3-р давхар' is 3rd floor and '305 тоот' is room 305.
Incorrect. The audio stated 3-р давхар.
Incorrect. The numbers do not match.

exercises.explanation: Mongolian uses '-р/-дугаар' for ordinal numbers (3-р = гуравдугаар) and 'тоот' (numbered unit) for office and apartment rooms.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Сайн байна! Floor and room number parsed accurately.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Listen for '3-р давхарт' (3rd floor) and '305 тоот' (room 305).

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: Ordinal numeral abbreviation in Cyrillic uses a hyphen followed by 'р' (1-р, 2-р, 3-р) or 'дугаар/дүгээр'.

audio.speechSynthesisText: Болд захирлын өрөө гуравдугаар давхарт, гурван зуун таван тоот.
audio.ipaTranscription: /pɔɮtʰ tsaxʲirɮiːŋ ɵrɵː ɢʊrəwtʊɢaːr tʰawxərtʰ, ɢʊrwəŋ tsʊːŋ tʰawəŋ tʰɔːtʰ/

exercises.prompt: The receptionist hands you a guest badge and says: 'Энэ зочны үнэмлэхийг зүүгээрэй' (Please wear this guest ID). What is the appropriate acknowledgment?
exercises.stimulusTextCyrillic: Хүлээн авагч: Энэ зочны үнэмлэхийг зүүгээрэй.
exercises.hint: Express gratitude and indicate you understand.

options.text: Маш их баярлалаа, ойлголоо. (Thank you very much, understood.)
options.explanation: Correct! 'Баярлалаа, ойлголоо' is the courteous and expected acknowledgment.

options.text: Үгүй, би зүүхгүй. (No, I won't wear it.)
options.explanation: Incorrect. Uncooperative and socially unacceptable.

options.text: Энэ юу вэ? Би явж байна. (What is this? I am leaving.)
options.cyrillic: Энэ юу вэ? Би явж байна.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Confused and inappropriate.

exercises.correctAnswer: Маш их баярлалаа, ойлголоо. (Thank you very much, understood.)
exercises.explanation: 'Маш их баярлалаа' followed by 'ойлголоо' (understood) completes the security check-in exchange smoothly.

learnerFeedback.onSuccess: Яг зөв! Seamless professional visitor etiquette.
learnerFeedback.onFailure: Respond with gratitude: 'Маш их баярлалаа, ойлголоо.'.

exercises.detailedGrammarNote: The verb ending '-аарай⁴' ('зүүгээрэй') is the prescriptive imperative expressing polite instructions or invitations from an authority/host.
